label: winner or champion of
definition: The first entity won the competition or award designated by the second, or held its championship title.
scope_notes: Win and winner dominate, using the same scope as rel_112 and the earlier reviews. Reaching or participating in an event, winning only a stage, and winning political office do not establish this competition/award predicate. A malformed appended path is not needed when clean direct evidence exists.

facts.reason: Ullrich directly wins the Tour and begins defending its championship. The stage win alone would not establish overall victory; the corrupted suffix and runner-up row are additional mixed evidence.
Clinton winning the White House refers to political office, and performance in it is another political/locative meaning. Neither is an award or competition championship under the preserved scope.
The Giants explicitly win the Super Bowl in three rows. Reaching it is weaker additional evidence, not the sole basis.
Both supplied paths directly say the Red Sox win the World Series. The evidence criterion does not independently establish historical date or recover missing modal modifiers.
There is explicit World Series win evidence for Yankees and Marlins, but the first latent entity combines those different team names. The participation row does not resolve the identity collision.
facts.reviewer_question: Does this first entity denote the Yankees or the Marlins, and should their World Series facts be separated?
